function.mechanism: Acts as an acidulant/acidity regulator by lowering food pH, contributing sourness and conditions that can inhibit growth of some microorganisms.

adi.basis: SCF ADI 0-6 mg/kg bw/day (opinion year 1990) as recorded in EFSA OpenFoodTox; critical effect nephrocalcinosis in rats, NOAEL 600 mg/kg bw/day with UF 100; EFSA food-additive re-evaluation process was active in 2024.

efsa.key_finding: E297 remains permitted in the EU, but EFSA re-evaluation is ongoing; preliminary EFSA exposure modelling (2024 background document) estimated high-end toddler intake up to 54.7 mg/kg bw/day under conservative assumptions.

adi.basis: Group ADI not specified for fumaric acid and its salts (established 1989; maintained at 53rd meeting in 1999).

concerns.summary: Historical SCF toxicological basis in EFSA OpenFoodTox identifies nephrocalcinosis in rats as the critical effect; ADI derived from a rat NOAEL of 600 mg/kg bw/day.

In EFSA's 2024 feed additive renewal opinion, fumaric acid was described as irritant to skin/eyes/respiratory tract and as skin/respiratory sensitiser in user-handling context; this is primarily occupational rather than dietary consumer exposure.
Recent safety alerts on fumaric acid esters (drug class) report severe GI adverse events, but these findings are indirect for E297 and not direct evidence of equivalent dietary additive risk.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA chemical record reports ADI 'not specified' (1989), maintained in 1999 with comment of no safety concern at current flavouring-use intake.
EFSA/JECFA background materials describe fumaric acid as a normal metabolic intermediate in the tricarboxylic acid cycle.
A PubMed-indexed packaging biocompatibility study reported no in vitro cytotoxicity in tested human keratinocyte assays for fumaric-acid-functionalized materials.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2024 preliminary conservative exposure estimates reached up to 54.7 mg/kg bw/day (95th percentile toddlers), which exceeds the historical SCF ADI of 0-6 mg/kg bw/day.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory approvals persist (EU/US; JECFA ADI not specified), but EFSA's historical SCF-based ADI is numerical and conservative exposure modelling indicates potential exceedance in children while EFSA re-evaluation remains incomplete.
key_factors: EU permitted status with ongoing EFSA re-evaluation
Historical SCF ADI 0-6 mg/kg bw/day in EFSA OpenFoodTox
JECFA group ADI not specified maintained in 1999
Conservative EFSA exposure estimates high in toddlers/children
No IARC carcinogenic group listing identified
